title: Bank Probationary Officer
summary: A bank probationary officer (PO) is a new Scale I officer in a public or private bank, hired through an entrance exam or a bank training programme. During a probation of about two years they rotate through branch desks such as accounts, cash, clearing and loans, reporting to the branch manager before being confirmed as an officer.
dailyDuties: Open savings, current and fixed deposit accounts after checking KYC documents
Supervise cash, cheque clearing and remittance work at the branch
Process retail and small business loan files under a senior officer
Resolve customer requests and complaints at the counter
Cross-sell deposits, loans, cards and insurance to meet branch targets
Prepare daily branch reports and compliance returns

skills.expectation: Handle deposit accounts, cash, cheque clearing and remittances under branch rules
Verify customer KYC documents when opening accounts and processing loans
Know RBI basics such as NPA classification and prudential norms
Read a borrower's balance sheet and work out basic ratios for a loan proposal
Resolve walk-in customer requests and complaints at the branch
Cross-sell deposits, loans, cards and insurance to meet branch targets
Keep branch reports and target trackers in Excel
Explain products and rules clearly to customers in English and the local language
Prepare appraisal notes for retail and MSME loans under a senior officer
Collect and check loan documents before sanction and disbursement
Post transactions and look up accounts in a core banking system such as Finacle
Bring in new savings, current and fixed deposit accounts
Follow PMLA and RBI KYC directions when flagging unusual transactions
Sell mutual funds and insurance once the required exam certificates are held
